result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_simple()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is simple (no self-loops or multi-edges). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3990-L4045){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_simple() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A simple graph contains no self-loops (edges from a node to itself) and no multi-edges (multiple edges between the same pair of nodes). This is a fundamental graph property used in many theoretical results. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is simple, `False` if it has self-loops or multi-edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Check if a graph is simple: ::: {#50d2173b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B") ) # Returns True graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cef787db .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Add a self-loop graph.add_edge("A", "A") # Returns False graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Multi-edges also make a graph non-simple: ::: {#9936b3ac .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("A", "B") # Duplicate edge (auto-assigned different IDs) ) # Returns False graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: :::
